Purpose: Shared tail-call landing that stages this tick's three rope sprites and then falls into the state-table dispatch at $107E. Inputs: no register is read here; the single JSR reads room_has_rope $0402, rope_animation_divider $1018, rope_oscillator_position $0403 and the pointer table at $1856. Both external callers arrive with A holding the byte just read from $D01E and with N and Z set from it ($1B08 in update_player_attached_to_rope, $1BAD in handle_rope_tile_collision), and with player_state $33 already forced to 2 and $51/$53 cleared; that A is dead because $107E immediately reloads $33. On the internal fallthrough from $1078 the registers are whatever attach_player_to_rope_if_colliding left. Outputs: on every second rope tick, staged sprite bytes $0500-$05BF, staged coordinates $05C0-$05C5, handshake $0407 = $FF and an advanced oscillator; then control falls through to $107E. Nothing returns to the caller. Assumptions: both external entries are JMP tail calls, so this block owns no return address. From $1B0B the surrounding state-6 handler was itself entered by JMP ($1011) at $108E and owns no frame either, so the topmost stack word still belongs to the game main loop; from $1BB0 the JSR return address pushed at $1B49, $1B4D, $1B52, $1B56, $1B5B or $1B5F is abandoned and never popped. Nothing unwinds it here: the stack pointer is reclaimed wholesale by the LDX #$FF / TXS at $3349 or $334F that terminates the tick. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, zero page $07, $08 and $31, and the rope staging state, all through produce_rope_sprite_staging. Hardware: the callers' reads of $D01E have already cleared the VIC-II sprite/sprite collision latch; produce_rope_sprite_staging sets sprite-enable bits 5-7 in $D015 and clears X-MSB bits 5-7 in $D010. The staged bytes only become visible to VIC-II when the raster IRQ copies them to $6B00-$6BBF at $353F.

Purpose: Select the handler for the current player state from the seven-entry table at $1003-$1010 and enter it through the mutable indirect target $1011. Inputs: player_state $33, which must be 0-6, and the table itself. No register input: A is reloaded from $33 at once, so the caller's A, X and flags are dead. The one external caller, $1B34 in update_player_attached_to_rope, arrives with A holding the byte just read from $D01E at $1B31 and with $33 already set to 1, jump direction $1013 copied from manual direction $49, and $52, $51 and $53 cleared - it is a jump-off-the-rope transition, not a state query. Outputs: writes the selected handler address into $1011/$1012 and jumps through it; control never returns here. Assumptions: the external entry is a JMP tail call, so this block owns no return address; state 6 was itself entered by JMP ($1011) and owns no frame, so the topmost stack word is still the game main loop's, and nothing between here and the LDX #$FF / TXS at $3349 or $334F unwinds it. The ASL/TAX index is unchecked, so a $33 above 6 would read past the table. Clobbers: A, X, flags, and the writable pointer $1011/$1012. Y is preserved into the handler. Hardware: none at this address; the entered handler may drive VIC-II, SID or CIA state.

Purpose: Two-instruction fork that sends grounded horizontal movement to the right-moving path at $10CC or the left-moving path at $112A according to the sign of the signed direction byte the caller has just loaded. Inputs: the N flag only. Internally $10C2 reaches here with N from LDA $49 at $10C0 and only when manual direction $49 is non-zero; externally $1535 in update_player_on_conveyor reaches here with N from LDA $13 at $1533, the room's signed conveyor direction, with no preceding zero test, so a $13 of $00 takes the BPL branch to $10CC. A itself is never re-read: both destinations reload from $32 and $4F. Outputs: control transfers to $10CC or $112A; no memory and no register is written. Assumptions: the external entry is a JMP tail call inside player state 4, and that handler was entered by JMP ($1011) at $108E, so no return address of state 4 or of this block is on the stack and the topmost stack word belongs to the game main loop. This block never reads $33, so it cannot and must not distinguish state 0 from state 4; the state-dependent part of grounded movement lives further on in handle_ground_support_tile $11C4, which does read $33. Clobbers: nothing - only PC changes. A, X, Y and all flags pass through unchanged. Hardware: none.

Purpose: Move the player one step to the right in grounded movement - advance the sub-cell phase and facing frame, cross into the next cell when the phase wraps, take the right-hand room exit at column $1F, and probe the tiles being entered. Inputs: player_horizontal_phase $32, player_x_cell $4F, facing frame $50, working tile row $0F, tile probe X $1014, and previous_exit_right $20 on the exit path. No register input: LDA $32 overwrites A on the first instruction. Internally $10C7 arrives with N clear; externally $15ED in enter_or_reconcile_conveyor arrives with A holding resolved_conveyor_direction $1017, known non-negative because $15E8 took BPL. Both values are dead. Outputs: updated $32 and $50, $4F incremented on a cell crossing, tile probes with grounded and ground-support handling; or, at column $1F with phase below 2, $0E loaded from $20, $33 = 2, $51 = 0, $53 = 0 followed by prepare_room_via_vector $1027. Every path leaves through $1021, $1027 or the shared continuation at $11B1; nothing returns. Assumptions: the external entry is a JMP tail call inside player state 5, which was entered by JMP ($1011) and owns no return address, so the topmost stack word is the game main loop's and this block must not attempt to RTS. Purpose: Discard the entire hardware stack with LDX #$FF / TXS and enter the player update at player_tick_entry $1000. It serves both as the tail of schedule_player_update's sixth-pass path and as the standing target of the player redispatch vector. Inputs: none in registers. X is overwritten immediately; A, Y and the flags carried in are never read. Externally it is entered through JMP ($CFF2) at redispatch_player_via_vector $101E, whose callers have just written a new player state to $33 and expect $1000 to dispatch it: $10BD and $15AB and $15E2 and $1530 set state 1, $119F sets state 3, $1580 and $1599 set state 4. $CFF2/$CFF3 hold $49/$33, that is $3349, stored by LDA #$49 / STA $CFF2 at $2D48-$2D4A and LDA #$33 / STA $CFF3 at $2D4D-$2D4F during initialize_game. Outputs: SP = $FF and control passes to $1000. It never returns and cannot: the return address of whatever called it has just been discarded. Assumptions: unusually for a routine entry, this block deliberately destroys its caller's stack frame and every frame beneath it. That is precisely the engine's mechanism for tolerating tail-jumps out of JSR-called helpers - $119F leaves handle_grounded_tile, entered by JSR from $110F, $1117, $116F and $1177, without ever executing its RTS, and $14BC leaves handle_horizontal_jump_collision the same way. Consequently nothing may be held on the stack across this address, it must never be reached by JSR expecting a return, and callers must have committed all state to memory before jumping. Only the stack pointer is reset; the bytes in page 1 are left as they are. Clobbers: X, set to $FF; SP, set to $FF; N and Z from the LDX. A, Y, C, V and all memory are untouched. Hardware: none. Interrupts are not masked here, so a raster IRQ taken immediately after the TXS pushes onto the freshly reset stack at $01FF downwards, which is the intended behaviour.

Retained loading-complete entry: installs failure cartridge vectors via $3C77, clears the KERNAL screen, initializes voice 3 and prints the message at $3C8F. It waits for a decoded key through $3A57, then enters the four-color code prompt at $3B20. This predecessor phase is separate from initialized gameplay.
Waits until keyboard scanner $3791 reports nonzero key count in $43. The scan runs with interrupts disabled; CLI precedes RTS.

Little-endian base word used at $3B65/$3B6C to fetch four expected color indexes. The captured image contains $2C57, inside the gameplay initializer. Do not substitute a protection-sheet table from another release; the origin of this captured base remains open.
High byte of the expected-color base word at $3A61. $3B6C adds it, with carry, to the high byte of four times the selected row/column cell offset.
Eight bytes loaded into sprite 0-3 X/Y registers at $3BC1/$3BC4; the X bytes are also used by the current-digit cursor at $3C15.
Current input slot, incremented and masked to 0-3 at $3C08-$3C10. Values entered with keys 1-4 are stored at $3A7D plus this index.
Eight sprite colors loaded at $3BBB; the first four are selected again when keys 1-4 enter their corresponding color indexes.
Zero at the initial loading-complete entry. A failed full code increments it then retries once; a subsequent failure branches to the permanent red-screen loop $3C6B.

Four entered color indexes. Initialization writes $FF for unset slots. $3C23 first rejects any negative byte as incomplete, then compares all four bytes with $3A81-$3A84. Positive, four individual mismatches and one unset-slot case were checked live.
Four expected values fetched indirectly by $3B73, each masked with $03. The captured checker accepts exactly these four bytes in order.
Upper bound saved by $3B12; oscillator-3 samples are masked with $1F and retried while greater than or equal to this bound.
Selected row 0-19 from $3B35. Its table offset is read from $3AE8 and its displayed row label from $3AC0.
Selected column 0-17 from $3B49. Added to the row offset, multiplied by four and added to the captured base at $3A61.
28-byte first-attempt prompt drawn by $3B84-$3B98 into $042E-$0449, with uppercase ASCII converted to screen codes.
28-byte retry prompt selected when $3A7C is nonzero; drawn into the same screen cells as the first prompt.
20 two-byte row labels, selected at $3BA8 by twice the chosen row and written to screen cells $044B-$044C.
Second-byte operand base for the 20 two-character row labels at $3AC0-$3AE7. $3BAE reads this base plus twice the selected row and writes the right-hand displayed character.
20 little-endian offsets indexed by twice the selected row at $3B3D/$3B42. The selected column is added before multiplying by four.

High-byte operand base for the 20 little-endian row offsets at $3AE8-$3B0F. $3B42 reads this base plus twice the chosen row. The following two bytes at $3B10-$3B11 are outside the indexed table and their meaning is open.

Additional row-offset word $0168, equal to 20 times 18. It continues the 18-byte stride sequence at $3AE8. The observed row selector rejects values >=20, so this final word is outside the selected indexes; no other consumer is established.
Samples SID oscillator-3 output, masks to five bits and rejects samples >= A. Called with $14 for the row and $12 for the column. No statistical distribution claim is made.
Waits for keys to clear, resets entered slots to $FF, selects the row/column and fetches four two-bit color values. Draws the prompt and sprite-based input display, then polls keys 1-4 and Return.
Accepts a single decoded key: Return enters $3C23; keys 1-4 store indexes 0-3 at the current slot and update its sprite pointer/color. Other keys return to polling.
Waits until no key is held, advances the slot modulo four, moves the cursor and resumes code input. An incomplete Return check also branches here.

First tests all four entered bytes with BMI for unset slots, then compares them in reverse index order against the four expected bytes. Exact match reaches $3C3A; any mismatch reaches $3C4E. Six controlled live cases agreed.
Installs success cartridge vectors via $3C83, waits for key release, clears five decoded-key bytes and jumps through $0FA0 with interrupts disabled.
On the first failure sets the retry flag and re-enters $3B20. With a nonzero retry flag, branches directly to the red-screen failure loop.
Nine-byte cartridge header copied to $8000 by $3C77: both entry vectors point to $3C6B, followed by the CBM80 signature.
Nine-byte cartridge header copied to $8000 by $3C83: both entry vectors point to $0FA0, followed by the CBM80 signature. All nine copied bytes matched in a controlled live call.
SEI, sets background and border to color 2, then loops to itself. This is the target of the retained failure cartridge entry vectors.
Copies nine bytes from $3C59-$3C61 into $8000-$8008, descending X=8..0, then returns.
Copies nine bytes from $3C62-$3C6A into $8000-$8008, descending X=8..0. Live output matched the entire source header.
40-byte ASCII loading-complete message. $3CB7 copies it to $0400-$0427, converting uppercase letters with AND $1F.
Draws the 40-byte message at $3C8F into KERNAL screen RAM $0400, from X=39 down to zero, converting uppercase ASCII to screen codes.
Repeatedly calls $3791 while decoded key count $43 is nonzero; then enables interrupts and returns.

Retained helper: sets port $36, source $07/$08=$B000, destination $09/$0A=$2000 and copies 32 pages ascending, then sets port $37 and returns. An isolated clone at $0200 copied all 8192 source bytes exactly. The original address lies inside its destination range, so that controlled relocation does not establish safe execution from the retained address or identify its earlier caller.
